title: A Decision Owner Stops Colleagues From Stonewalling
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece examines how consensus-driven teams can be paralyzed by a single member who habitually stalls decisions through endless requests for more data or debate. The author argues that most teams tolerate this because they value everyone feeling comfortable with a decision, allowing one dissenter to hold the group hostage indefinitely. The fix proposed is naming a designated decision owner in advance of any major choice, so that after full debate a single person or role can break a logjam. This owner is not meant to dominate the process but to serve as a tiebreaker only when consensus genuinely cannot be reached. The article frames this as a structural safeguard rather than a personality fix, since it removes the leverage of chronic obstructors without requiring conflict. It closes by asking readers to check whether ownership is clearly assigned on their own teams.
points: A single team member can indefinitely stall group decisions by demanding more data, clarity, or debate.
Teams that prize consensus often let one dissenter block progress rather than confront them directly.
Naming a decision owner in advance prevents any one person from being able to stonewall the group.
The decision owner's role is narrow: they only make the final call when consensus genuinely cannot be reached.
Establishing ownership before deliberation begins encourages fuller, fairer engagement from everyone.
quotes: Disruptive team members learn to use the group’s desire for consensus to block, delay, postpone, or stonewall a decision.
It only takes one selfish team member to obstruct the group.
After debate, discussion, and full engagement of a decision, when consensus can’t be reached, the decision owner makes the call.
This owner has no other expanded role in the decision process except to break any logjam.
By establishing a decision owner for every major decision, good leaders don’t allow any one team member to ever obstruct the group.
On the best teams, the decision owner rarely has to make the call.
